NoteTexAccessor::strip_bib¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::strip_bib() const

Remove Bibliography Machinery As Complete Units¶

strip_bib() removes complete \bibliography{...} and \addbibresource{...} calls, \printbibliography with or without options, and complete thebibliography environments. It is intended for source views that retain surrounding prose but must exclude bibliography configuration and authored reference-list bodies.

Required and optional groups are balanced, so braces inside a resource path or option do not terminate a call early. Same-name bibliography environments are depth balanced and removed as one outer region. Escaped commands, longer control words, incomplete required groups, and unclosed environments remain unchanged rather than causing partial deletion.

After removal, ASCII whitespace is collapsed and the cell is trimmed. This prevents holes left by deleted regions, but means the operation is not a byte-preserving splice. It is lane-wise, out-of-place, and shape preserving; empty results remain empty cells. Undefined input stays undefined and defined non-Text Notes are rejected. The balanced scan is linear in source bytes and allocates one result string per cell.

Example 1: Commands, Options, And Nested Environments¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(Before \bibliography{refs/{main}} middle \printbibliography[heading={none}] after)",
    R"(A \begin{thebibliography}{9} one \begin{thebibliography}{1} nested \end{thebibliography} two \end{thebibliography} Z)",
    R"(\\bibliography{escaped} \bibliography{unfinished)"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_bib() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["Before middle after", "A Z", "\\\\bibliography{escaped} \\bibliography{unfinished"]

The first two lanes remove complete structures. The escaped and malformed forms in the third lane are preserved.

Example 2: Higher-Rank Input, Allocation, And Idempotence¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(A \addbibresource{refs/a.bib} B)",
                             R"(\printbibliography)", "plain", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto clean = grid.tex().strip_bib();
std::cout << clean << '\n';
std::cout << "shape=[" << clean.size(0) << ", " << clean.size(1) << "]\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "receiver unchanged="
          << (grid.at(0).find("addbibresource") != std::string_view::npos)
          << " idempotent=" << ((clean == clean.tex().strip_bib()).all().bool_item())
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["A B", ""], 
  ["plain", ""]
]
shape=[2, 2]
receiver unchanged=true idempotent=true

The empty result from \printbibliography remains a cell; it is not removed from the tensor. The unchanged receiver and idempotent result make the method safe to place in a repeatable cleanup pipeline.

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_bib().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().strip_bib();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip bib Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
strip bib Int64: rejected
